chunks: They said: "O Moses, we shall never enter it so long as they are in it. Go you and your Lord and fight; we will sit here."
ai.seo_question: What did the children of Israel say to Moses when they refused to enter the promised land?
ai.summary: In this verse from Surah Al-Ma'idah, the Israelites' refusal to enter Canaan reveals a profound spiritual stagnation where they demanded Moses and God fight their battle, effectively shifting responsibility for divine promise onto the Prophet. Shia exegetes, such as Al-Tabarsi and Al-Kulayni, highlight this as a paradigm of 'inaction despite capability,' contrasting their passive waiting with the active struggle (Jihad) required of the faithful. This incident underscores the theological principle that divine aid is contingent upon human effort and readiness, rather than mere expectation.
